vocabulary.example: Which season do you like best?

grammar.explanation_en: Use the preposition 'in' before months and seasons: 'in July', 'in summer', 'in winter'. This is different from days, which use 'on' (on Monday), and specific times, which use 'at' (at three o'clock).
grammar.explanation_ko: 월과 계절 앞에는 전치사 'in'을 씁니다: 'in July'(7월에), 'in summer'(여름에), 'in winter'(겨울에). 요일 앞에는 'on'(on Monday), 구체적인 시각 앞에는 'at'(at three o'clock)을 쓰는 것과 다릅니다.

examples.en: It snows a lot in winter.
School starts in March in Korea.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: Which season do you like the most?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: I like fall. The weather is cool and nice.
dialogue.line_ko: 저는 가을을 좋아해요. 날씨가 시원하고 좋아요.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: When does fall begin in Korea?

reading.title: Four Seasons
reading.text: Korea has four seasons. Spring begins in March and is warm. Summer starts in June and is very hot. Fall begins in September, and the weather becomes cool. Winter starts in December and is cold, with snow.
reading.text_ko: 한국에는 사계절이 있어요. 봄은 3월에 시작하고 따뜻해요. 여름은 6월에 시작하고 아주 더워요. 가을은 9월에 시작하고 날씨가 시원해져요. 겨울은 12월에 시작하고 춥고 눈이 와요.

explanation.en: The text says 'Spring begins in March.'
The text says summer 'is very hot.'
The text says winter is cold, 'with snow.'
